subject: Business Models
title: Salesforce and Cloud SaaS
description: A quick, practical guide to Salesforce and Cloud SaaS.

hook.text: In 1999, Salesforce launched with a radical slogan: 'No Software.' Everything lived in the cloud.

buildup.text: Traditional software meant buying CDs, installing updates, and maintaining servers. Salesforce eliminated all of that.

discovery.text: Monthly subscriptions gave customers lower upfront costs and automatic updates. Salesforce grew explosively.

twist.text: Salesforce's revenue is 95% recurring. Investors value it at 8x revenue because that income is predictable.

climax.text: Salesforce proved SaaS works. It inspired thousands of cloud startups and killed boxed software forever.

punchline.text: No CDs, no servers, just pay monthly. Salesforce changed software forever.

quiz.question: What percentage of Salesforce's revenue is recurring?

details.summary: Salesforce pioneered the cloud SaaS subscription model when Marc Benioff launched it in 1999 with the slogan 'No Software.' By delivering CRM through web browsers with monthly subscriptions instead of expensive installed software.
details.whyItMatters: Salesforce's model proved that enterprise software could be delivered as a subscription service, inspiring thousands of SaaS companies..
takeaways: Cloud delivery replaced expensive on-premise software installations
Monthly subscriptions replaced large upfront license purchases
Salesforce's model became the template for the entire SaaS industry

faq.question: How did Salesforce convince enterprises to adopt cloud subscriptions?
faq.answer: No hardware to buy, no software to install, no IT staff needed for maintenance. Updates happened automatically. Companies could start small and expand gradually. The total cost of ownership was lower than traditional on-premise CRM despite seemingly higher per-seat pricing.

faq.question: Why did the SaaS subscription model spread across enterprise software?
faq.answer: Vendors preferred predictable recurring revenue over lumpy license sales. Investors valued SaaS companies at higher multiples due to revenue predictability. Customers preferred operational expenses over capital expenses. Cloud infrastructure made delivery costs negligible at scale.
